text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents original research applying a participatory framework to develop spatially explicit, national-scale land use and land cover change (LULCC) scenarios for mainland Tanzania to 2025 under two distinct future pathways—business as usual (BAU) and green economy (GE). It meets all core inclusion criteria: (1) explicit national-scale implementation covering the entire Tanzanian mainland (~883,600 km²); (2) LULC prediction is the central research objective, with scenarios built to model future LULCC dynamics; (3) two quantitative future scenarios are developed and compared, with detailed estimates of land conversion (e.g., +53,867 km² cropland in BAU vs. +44,132 km² in GE) and degradation areas; (4) spatial modeling integrates stakeholder-derived likelihood scores with national datasets to produce composite indicators and allocate land demand across pixels; and (5) outputs include mapped national projections of LULCC (e.g., Fig. 3 and 4). The study does not fall under any exclusion criteria—it is not global, local, or regional only; it includes explicit LULC prediction; it is not species- or carbon-focused without LULC analysis; and it goes beyond qualitative or single-scenario work. Although participatory, the modeling yields quantitative, spatially explicit national maps with reported change rates and areas, fulfilling all requirements for 'OK'.)
